findings.title: Block-hit stats are rolled back on the signup they record
findings.body: BlockedEmail.should_block? increments match_count and last_match_at and calls record.save while it is invoked from EmailValidator during User validation. User#save runs validations inside the same database transaction, and a blocked address fails validation, so that transaction rolls back and undoes the BlockedEmail update. On a normal install (SiteSetting.call_discourse_hub? false) UsersController#create only calls save, so blocked signup attempts never persist match statistics — last_match_at stays nil and match_count stays 0, which is the signal the model spec says admins use to see whether a rule has ever matched. When call_discourse_hub? is true, create calls user.valid? (line 168) before save, so the first increment commits and the second is rolled back, and the counter moves by 1 instead of 2. The write has to happen outside the user transaction (separate connection, or after the user save/rollback), or the stats feature does not work for the block action.

findings.title: Exact email match lets blocked addresses sign up
findings.body: should_block? loads BlockedEmail with a case-sensitive where(email: email) and never strips or downcases. Signup stores whatever was posted (User.new_from_params assigns params[:email] raw), while change_email in UsersController canonicalizes with Email.downcase(...).strip. A row for user@evil.com therefore does not match User@evil.com, user@evil.com with surrounding whitespace, or other case variants, so the new block is bypassed by changing case or padding the address. Uniqueness on blocked_emails.email is also case-sensitive, so both casings can be stored and .first can return either row. Normalize on write (set_defaults) and on lookup the same way change_email does, and compare the normalized value, or the blocklist does not actually block.

findings.title: match_count increment loses updates under concurrency
findings.body: The hit counter is read-modify-write: match_count += 1 followed by save. Two overlapping signup attempts that match the same blocked row both read the same count and both write count+1, so one hit is dropped. Popular blocked addresses are exactly the rows that get concurrent attempts. Even after the stat update is moved out of the user transaction, this still needs an atomic update (for example update_all("match_count = match_count + 1") on that id) rather than loading the integer into Ruby.

findings.title: Tests stub the block check and miss signup behavior
findings.body: EmailValidator examples stub BlockedEmail.should_block?, so they never hit the database, never assert the user.email.blocked message, and never run User#save. BlockedEmail specs only call should_block? directly, which commits the counter outside a user transaction, so they stay green while a real blocked signup rolls the stats back and while a case or whitespace variant is allowed through. There is also no coverage that the domain whitelist/blacklist logic moved out of User still rejects addresses. A User create/save example with a real BlockedEmail row (including a different-case address) is needed or these failures ship untested.
